doc.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021

title: Drinking and drugs in jazz
summary: Asked about Bill Evans and drug use, Israels says he can't explain it and that it faded over his career.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I’m not going to spend a lot of time on this but you, in a fairly recent interview which I thought was done very well from a fellow out there, you spoke about being in a hotel room with Bill Evans and watching him basically shoot up and I’m wondering why the drinking and the drugs has been associated with jazz. I’m sure it’s overblown but you are saying it was part of the scene. Do you know why?

No. Maybe just staying up late at night, I’m not sure. I’m going to close the door so I don’t hear the practicing the flute too much. Okay. I don’t really know the answer to that. That’s someone else’s area of expertise. And interestingly it has totally evaporated from — you know as I went through my jazz career the presence of drugs and drinking diminished, diminished, diminished, diminished to the point where everybody was healthy people and vegetarians and exercisers, a lot smarter.
